seo.name: Matheapolis
seo._name: The wordmark on its own, for og:site_name (src/layouts/Layout.astro). The club was the Minneapolis Math Book Club until 2026-11-07, when the operator rebranded it: "I want the focus on the people and the ideas more than the book. the book is more an inspiration". A site_name that carries a descriptor makes two claims in the field a platform uses to label its source, so the descriptor lives in "title" instead. Do not use this slot to rename the Meetup group or the Mobilizon group - those are other organisations' records, listed in design/grill/copy-options.mjs as ORG_OF_RECORD.
seo.title: Matheapolis - a Minneapolis–St. Paul math club
seo._title: Was 'Join the Minneapolis Math Book Club | Math Book Discussions' — an imperative and a keyword phrase, in the voice of a listing rather than the club. og:title and twitter:title read this slot, and it is what a search result bolds, so it is the wordmark plus the descriptor. The descriptor names both cities from 2026-11-08 (operator: say “Minneapolis-St. Paul Math Club” rather than “Twin Cities Math Club”, because the club's name is a play on the city's name — `Math` inside `Minneapolis` — and a descriptor that says “Twin Cities” never prints the city the wordmark puns on); it is the same phrase the hero's label lane carries, with the article kept because a title is read as a sentence fragment and the lane is a label. Both forms were measured in the lane's own face and case: 257px of ink with the article, 243.7px without, in a 288px lane at 320, one line box either way @measured 2026-11-08 by `npm run round16`. The 2026-11-07 ruling this slot carried (“A Twin Cities math club”) is recorded in `src/components/HeroSection.astro` and D240. It does NOT carry the old name: the continuity line is in the hero copy, where a person reads it, and the old apex keeps serving rather than 404ing, which is what actually preserves six years of links (D112's locator rule, applied to metadata). The share card is not a slot for this ruling — its kicker already prints “Minneapolis, MN” (scripts/make-social-share.mjs).
seo.description: A math club in Minneapolis and St. Paul. We work through papers, proofs, proof assistants and puzzles together, around a table in a coffee shop or a brewery. Dates and sign-up on Meetup; the discussion runs in the chat.
seo._description: Was 'Connect with fellow math lovers in our vibrant reading community. Monthly meetups, engaging discussions, and diverse book selections in Minneapolis, MN.' — 'vibrant', 'engaging' and 'diverse' are unsourced adjectives, and 'diverse book selections' describes a service the club does not run (2026-11-03). No cadence word here: the one cadence claim the site makes is the hero label, and it carries its source in src/content.json (D92). This sentence is also what a link unfurl shows, so it is written for a person. Re-read it when the venues or the paths change; `check:content` scans <meta content> for cadence words, so adding one means adding a source. 2026-11-08: “in the Twin Cities” became “in Minneapolis and St. Paul” for the same reason the lane changed — the descriptor is where the pun on the city name becomes readable. The cities it names are the venues the page already sources in src/content.json (Minneapolis, St. Paul and the surrounding area), so no new claim is made here.
